title: Thickenings and first order thickenings
statement: Let $T'$ be a scheme and $T\subset T'$ a closed subscheme, i.e. a scheme $T$ with a closed immersion $i:T\to T'$ [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]; the *ideal sheaf* of $T$ in $T'$ is the quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals $\mathcal I=\ker(\mathcal O_{T'}\to i_*\mathcal O_T)\subset\mathcal O_{T'}$. The scheme $T'$ is a *thickening* of $T$ if $T$ is a closed subscheme of $T'$ and the underlying topological spaces of $T$ and $T'$ are equal. It is a *first order thickening* of $T$ if $T$ is a closed subscheme of $T'$ and its ideal sheaf $\mathcal I$ has square zero, $\mathcal I^2=0$. It is a *finite order thickening* of $T$ if $T$ is a closed subscheme of $T'$ and $\mathcal I$ is nilpotent, i.e. $\mathcal I^{n+1}=0$ for some integer $n\geq0$; an *$n$th order thickening* if $\mathcal I^{n+1}=0$. (A first order or finite order thickening is a thickening: a nilpotent ideal sheaf cuts out the whole underlying space.) If $S$ is a scheme, a thickening $T\subset T'$ *over $S$* is one together with a morphism $T'\to S$ (so $T$ is over $S$ by composition with $i$), and it is a thickening *of affine schemes* if $T'$ is affine (and then so is $T$, a closed subscheme of an affine scheme).
